card_description: Ask for help or report a problem with a CAIL tool or service. Requires an activated CAIL Ticketing account.
heading: Using CAIL Ticketing
intro: CAIL Ticketing is where the Lab tracks help requests, bug reports, accessibility problems, and service interruptions. Students in a course that uses Lab tools should ask their instructor first.

steps.title: Register
steps.description: Create a CAIL Ticketing account. It is separate from your CUNY Login.

steps.title: Wait for activation
steps.description: CAIL staff review and activate new accounts manually, so you cannot sign in right away.

steps.title: Set up two-factor authentication
steps.description: The first time you sign in, set up two-factor authentication with an authenticator app.

steps.title: Open a ticket
steps.description: Submit your request in the CAIL Support project. Only you and CAIL staff can see the tickets you submit.

email_intro: Once your account is active, you can also open a ticket by email. Write to
email_details: from the email address on your CAIL Ticketing account. The subject becomes the ticket title and the message becomes its description. Mail from any other address does not create a ticket. To add to an existing ticket, reply to its notification email.
safety_note: Do not include passwords, API keys, access tokens, private research data, or other sensitive personal information in a ticket. Give the minimum useful description; the CAIL team will arrange a safer follow-up channel when needed.
fallback_text: Waiting for an account or unable to sign in? Email
